title: The fibrewise unramified locus is open and base-change compatible
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $W_h$ be the union of all opens $O\subseteq Z$ on which $h|_O$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $W_h$ is open and is precisely the set of $z\in Z$, $s=h(z)$, where the fibre $Z_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is unramified at $z$, meaning it has an unramified source neighbourhood in that fibre. Equivalently, $\mathcal O_{Z_s,z}=\kappa(z)$ via the residue map and $\kappa(z)/\kappa(s)$ is finite separable [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For any base change $h':Z'=Z\times_SS'\to S'$ with projection $g':Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product], one has $W_{h'}=(g')^{-1}(W_h)$. No flatness or local finite presentation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0475 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified), first assertion; the pointwise residue-field and fibre-local-ring characterization is Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), (1), (2) and (6).

proof.text: The locus is open directly from its definition: an unramified open neighbourhood of a point is contained in the locus. For a locally finite type morphism, membership in this locus is equivalent to formal unramifiedness of its actual stalk map. The forward implication uses the stalk map of the open restriction and cancels its isomorphism; the converse applies lem-sbc-formally-unramified-stalk-neighbourhood and the Mathlib open-diagonal criterion for a locally finite type formally unramified morphism.

source.place: Tag 02GF, equivalence (1) with (3) and openness proof

proof.text: Prove arbitrary-base-change compatibility on affine neighbourhoods. For a finite module M over A and a prime q of an A-algebra B, q belongs to the support of B tensor_A M exactly when its contraction belongs to the support of M. Use Mathlib Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct, tensor associativity, and faithful flatness of the extension kappa(p) to kappa(q). Apply this to the finite module of Kahler differentials and Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquiv; Algebra.unramifiedLocus_eq_compl_support gives the ring-level pointwise equivalence for a pushout. Choose affine opens in the base and the two factors containing the images of a point of the scheme pullback. Their inverse-image intersection is affine and its section square is a pushout. Mathlib arrowStalkMapIso identifies the actual stalk maps with the localizations of the affine section maps. Composition with the formally unramified localization of the base identifies formal unramifiedness over the localized base with formal unramifiedness over the original affine base. The ring-level equivalence and the membership criterion of step 1 therefore give the equality of loci. Locally finite type persists under base change by lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change. Specialize this equality to Spec kappa(h(z)) and the canonical point h.asFiber z; the first projection maps it to z, giving the fibrewise clause.

source.place: Tag 0475, differential base-change and residue-vector-space argument; Tag 02GF (3)--(5)

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion directly to h at z, retaining its finite separable residue-field condition unchanged. By lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient, the canonical map from the source stalk to the fibre stalk is surjective and has kernel m_s O_Z,z. It is a local homomorphism. Hence contraction of the fibre maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal, and injectivity of ideal contraction along a surjection shows that the fibre maximal ideal is zero exactly when m_s O_Z,z is the source maximal ideal. The canonical residue map of the fibre stalk is always surjective; it is an isomorphism exactly when its kernel, the maximal ideal, is zero. Combining these equivalences gives the residue-map clause without transporting residue-field extensions between the fibre and the source.

lean.statement: theorem unramifiedLocus_baseChange {Z S : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] : IsOpen (unramifiedLocus h) ∧ (∀ z : Z, z ∈ unramifiedLocus h ↔ h.asFiber z ∈ unramifiedLocus (h.fiberToSpecResidueField (h z))) ∧ (∀ z : Z, z ∈ unramifiedLocus h ↔ IsIso ((h.fiber (h z)).residue (h.asFiber z)) ∧ (h.residueFieldMap z).hom.Finite ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (h z)) (Z.residueField z) _ _ (h.residueFieldMap z).hom.toAlgebra) ∧ (∀ {S' : Scheme.{u}} (k : S' ⟶ S), unramifiedLocus (pullback.snd h k) = (pullback.fst h k) ⁻¹' unramifiedLocus h)
